builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
summary: The method replaces uniform (flat) bit-width allocation for MoE expert FFN tensors with layer-wise allocation derived from routing statistics (entropy, CV, Jaccard phase-fragility, top-1 strength), tuned by coordinate descent under a fixed average bpw budget. It costs a custom routing-capture and profiling pipeline in a modified inference runtime plus tuning compute, with no measured quality benefit over uniform quantization. What fails is the core premise: routing behavior is an unvalidated proxy for per-layer quantization cost, so guided allocation performs no better than random reallocation, and aggressive budgets lose quality regardless of allocation strategy.
rationale: The paper is a replicated negative result showing this approach does not beat the simpler uniform baseline, so a production team should keep uniform mixed-precision quantization and avoid investing in routing-profiling infrastructure.

claims.statement: The method replaces uniform (flat) bit-width allocation for MoE expert FFN tensors with layer-wise allocation derived from routing statistics (entropy, CV, Jaccard phase-fragility, top-1 strength), tuned by coordinate descent under a fixed average bpw budget. It costs a custom routing-capture and profiling pipeline in a modified inference runtime plus tuning compute, with no measured quality benefit over uniform quantization. What fails is the core premise: routing behavior is an unvalidated proxy for per-layer quantization cost, so guided allocation performs no better than random reallocation, and aggressive budgets lose quality regardless of allocation strategy.

No improvement claim: routing-guided reallocation fails to outperform uniform-bitrate baselines; neutral in the flat regime (z ~0.9), and at ~2.7 bpw random reallocation matches routing-guided allocation while the tier itself shows a decisive quality loss (z > 4 SE) replicated across three weight vectors.
